precepts.text: Be in pain, and labour to bring forth, O daughter of Zion, like a woman in travail. No matter what we are going through, we must be in pain and do this work to bring forth the kingdom.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
“For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his.” Paul is making a comparison between our works and God’s. God worked, then rested; so must we. Micah shows the labour: “Be in pain, and labour to bring forth, O daughter of Zion, like a woman in travail: for now shalt thou go forth out of the city.”

No matter what we are going through, brothers and sisters, we have to be in pain and do this work. Be in pain to bring forth the kingdom of heaven on earth.

That is why Paul says “Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief.” Labour, labour in pain, bring forth your works to enter into that rest, which is the kingdom. Rest is entered by labour. The generation in the wilderness fell because of unbelief; the daughter of Zion must travail to bring forth.

note.label: Cyber Warfare: The Mouth Of The Beast

precepts.why:
Paul and Barnabas went about “Confirming the souls of the disciples, and exhorting them to continue in the faith, and that we must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom of God.” The tribulation hasn't fully started; you see it on a certain scale, but it will intensify. It will get worse, and worse, and worse.

Micah says how to go through it: “Be in pain, and labour to bring forth, O daughter of Zion, like a woman in travail”. The Bible says to be in pain. Pain is coming, and it has already begun; pay attention to what Trump and these people are doing. But whatever pain you go through, you still have to labour, labouring in this truth.

“for now shalt thou go forth out of the city, and thou shalt dwell in the field, and thou shalt go even to Babylon”. Where are we living today? Babylon: Mystery Babylon the Great, the United States of America.

Why does it say like a woman in travail? Because the pain comes and it goes, and when the baby is close to coming the pains increase and get worse and worse. That is what you see taking place now. Whether this society has another ten or twenty years, as the time draws nearer the pains will increase: the affliction rising against those of us that fear God. Keep labouring through them.

That is why the brother who is not studying and applying the scriptures has no root and will not survive it; when things get real he will be offended, scared, and go back into the world. Sisters, a brother who never teaches and is never in a camp video is a gamble.

We cannot sit back knowing Christ is coming and not do the work; the time is short, and this is not our rest. The slack spirit of Joshua 18 has to go: we have to be in pain and labour to bring our brothers and sisters to repentance.

note.label: Psalm 46: God Is Our Refuge and Maketh Wars to Cease

precepts.why:
“Come, behold the works of the Lord, what desolations he hath made in the earth. He maketh wars to cease unto the end of the earth”. Micah puts the time on it: “in the last days it shall come to pass, that the mountain of the house of the Lord shall be established in the top of the mountains”, and many nations shall say “Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, and to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths: for the law shall go forth of Zion, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.” Then: “he shall judge among many people, and rebuke strong nations afar off; and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks: nation shall not lift up a sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.”

That is the breaking of the bow and the cutting of the spear. It is in the last days, when he rebukes strong nations afar off and the law goes forth of Zion, and it has not come yet; we are still in the wars and rumours of wars. The God of Jacob, whose house the nations will go up to, is our refuge.

“Be in pain, and labour to bring forth”: the Lord don’t care about your battle fatigue. Everybody’s tired, we’re trying to get out of captivity, and he says be in pain and labour to bring forth. “O daughter of Zion”: that’s a message to us. “Like a woman in travail”: work like a woman in travail.

“For now shalt thou go forth out of the city”: we left out of the city of Israel. “And thou shalt dwell in the field, and thou shalt go even to Babylon”. That’s the same thing the angel told Zechariah: the ephah with the woman is carried to build it an house in the land of Shinar, Babylon.

“There shalt thou be delivered”: we’re going to be delivered from this place here.

To be driven out: James writes “to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad.” That scattered abroad means driven out. We’ve been driven out, scattered worldwide, and our goal, our mission, is to assemble the twelve tribes. Everyone needs to understand that.

How God afflicted us. “The fruit of thy land, and all thy labours, shall a nation which thou knowest not eat up”: the nations eat up all our labors, all our work, all our resources. Everything we put our hand to the plow for, they reap the benefits. It goes with what was said about Lazarus, how the dogs would come and lick his wounds.

“And thou shalt be only oppressed and crushed alway”: that’s the part right there. That is our life. We’re the ones that God has afflicted, from slavery, oppression, colonialism.

God is only gathering a remnant. “In all the land, saith the Lord, two parts therein shall be cut off and die”: two-thirds of us will die in this land here, “but the third shall be left therein.”

“And I will bring the third part through the fire”: that is twofold, spiritual and literal. “And will refine them as silver is refined”: in a spiritual sense we’re being refined right now when he teaches us his laws, by keeping the commandments. We have our ups and downs, ins and outs, our trials and shortcomings, but we rise and get back up.

Literally, when we come through the fire he refines us; that’s him pleading with us face to face, and he’s going to teach us the laws, and it’s do or die on that day. It ain’t no ‘oh I committed adultery today, I’m sorry, forgive me.’ Nope, you dead. Rehearsal time is up, it’s over, it’s finished. That’s when he brings us under the bond of the covenant you read about in Ezekiel chapter 20. Right now we’re under the New Covenant, called grace.

About that first dominion: “He shall have dominion also from sea to sea, and from the river unto the ends of the earth.” Christ shall have dominion. That’s the first dominion, the great dominion, the dominion of Christ that comes to the tower of the flock, Jerusalem.

This is why the apostles asked this question that the churches ignore: “Lord, wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel?” The kingdom is only for Israel. They asked, is this the time, Lord? And Christ said the time is not for you to know yet.

So the kingdom shall come to the daughter of Jerusalem, and the kingdom ain’t for all nations, the kingdom ain’t for all races. The kingdom’s only for the Israelites.

There is a divine purpose behind all these deaths. Parents will ask, why Lord, why is this happening? “I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence”: our people refuse to acknowledge that as the Israelites we have sinned.

“And seek my face”: our people refuse to seek God’s face as the Israelites. To seek his face means you got to open his Bible and read the Bible with Israelite eyes and see yourself. You are the people of the book, but our people don’t want to do that.

“In their affliction they will seek me early.” That’s why there’s a reason behind all these deaths, and it’s only going to escalate.

Some of you think online the Democrats will save us; some of you think the Republicans will save us. Sad and bad news for all of you: none of them can save us. The deaths of our sons and daughters will only escalate until we acknowledge our offense; that’s what the Bible says.

“As for us, our eyes as yet failed for our vain help: in our watching we have watched for a nation that could not save us.” Every generation there’s a new group of negroes who got a bright idea: let’s be Democrats, or let’s be Republicans, or let’s be conservatives, let’s be something in the system. Somebody tell the Christians: the white man can’t save us. His political parties can’t save us. His false religions can’t save us. The Bible prophesies it: we have watched for a nation that could not save us.

Be in pain: no matter what we lose, we must continue and push, because we believe this. “Thy brother shall rise again”: your brother, your loved one, shall rise again. Martha said, “I know that he shall rise again in the resurrection at the last day.”

“I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live: And whosoever liveth and believeth in me shall never die.” Whosoever liveth and believeth in him means you keeping the commandments in the faith of Christ.

“Believest thou this?” That is the question we all have to answer: do you believe that?

Labor to bring forth the remnant of Israel. “Give diligence to make your calling and election sure.” Why give diligence? “For if ye do these things, ye shall never fall”: if you give diligence in God’s work, you shall never fall. We got to believe that thing.

“But watch thou in all things”: don’t just watch the news; watch in your own home, watch in your local congregations, watch what’s going on. “Endure afflictions”: endure whatever comes your way; we all must endure afflictions.

“Do the work of an evangelist”: don’t just sit home on your computer. If you sick and ailing we understand that, but if you are strong and able bodied, the Bible says you men do the work of an evangelist. Five brothers here don’t have a driver’s license. There may be reasons, child support or whatever, but don’t be a lazy brother. On one of our first trips we drove to Canada and took turns driving, and the black ninja sat in the back seat eating Kentucky Fried Chicken. When it was his turn to drive: I don’t know how to drive. Thirty-five years old with no driver’s license, simple as hell. On a simple mission to drive to Canada he just sat there going and coming eating chicken. That’s a useless brother; you’re useless.

That’s the basic driver’s license; from there, the passport. If you can’t travel on a plane, you can at least get in a cab, or get on the train and go locally and be a local prophet; there’s no shame in that, stay right there in your little community. But if you want to go where no man has gone before, do the work of an evangelist.

“Make full proof of thy ministry”: you have to make full proof of your ministry. Just having fringes on is not making full proof of your ministry. That’s not about the brother who is sick or handicapped; the Lord got them, that’s a special breed, they do what they can. It’s about able brothers who just sit around and scratch and eat chicken and watch porn. That’s who this is talking to.

This all covers be in pain, and labor, and labor, and labor to bring forth. “And though the Lord give you the bread of adversity”: because we going to be afflicted here, we going to catch hell. “And the water of affliction”: we cry at the things we see and the things we go through. That’s the water of affliction: our tears, our wives’ tears, our sons’ and daughters’ tears.

“Yet shall not thy teachers be removed into a corner any more”: why? Because your teachers will make full proof of their ministry; they will go where no man has gone before. “But thine eyes shall see thy teachers”: you going to see the men and say these are the men of God, these are the only men that’s taking that Bible serious.

“And thine ears shall hear a word behind thee”: behind thee, because some of our people are walking in the wrong direction, walking away from this truth. “Saying, This is the way, walk ye in it”: brothers and sisters, this is the way. “When ye turn to the right hand, and when ye turn to the left”: when you turn to the right hand you’re going to hear this truth, and when you turn to the left you’re going to hear this truth, because this truth will cover this earth.

“I will make thine horn iron”: he’s going to give us power. “Until the Ancient of days came”: until the time that God came, “and judgment was given to the saints of the most High.” The judgment that’s given to us is power. Right now we weak as hell; we can’t come against China, we can’t even come against the ones on the corner. The Lord said I got to give you power; judgment must be given to you.

“And the time came that the saints possessed the kingdom”: that’s the judgment. The time came that the saints possessed this planet Earth.

“Thou shalt beat in pieces many people”: that’s what Christ said. So what Bible is Jamal Bryant reading, what Bible are the Seventh Day Adventists and the Christians reading?

“And he that overcometh, and keepeth my works”: to keep Christ’s works means keep his commandments, “unto the end.” We got to keep them works unto the end. “To him will I give power over the nations.” It’s a hard thing for blacks and Latinos to comprehend, because we ain’t never had nothing, we ain’t never been nothing; we can’t conceive that we are God’s special and anointed people.

“And he shall rule them with a rod of iron”: we going to rule the nations with a rod of iron; we ain’t going to play with them. “As the vessels of a potter shall they be broken to shivers”: that’s that thresh we just read in Micah 4. “Even as I received of my Father”: the same rulership Christ got, he said I’m going to give it to you, because according to Romans 8 we are joint heirs with Christ.

“I will consecrate their gain unto the Lord.” “Therefore thy gates shall be open continually; they shall not be shut day nor night”: the gates of Jerusalem shall be opened continually, morning or evening time, “that men may bring unto thee the forces of the Gentiles.” That’s the gain consecrated from the nations: the forces of the Gentiles is their wealth. “And that their kings may be brought”: we going to bring their kings too.

“For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish”: any rebellious kingdom out there. “Yea, those nations shall be utterly wasted.”

“And he carried me away in the spirit to a great and high mountain”: the same mountain we just read about in Micah 4:1. “And shewed me that great city”, the great city of Micah 4:1, “the holy Jerusalem, descending out of heaven from God, Having the glory of God”.

It “had a wall great and high, and had twelve gates”, and “the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel” written on them. “The length and the breadth and the height of it are equal”: as long as it is, it’s going to be that high. It’s going to be huge, gigantic.

“And the nations of them which are saved shall walk in the light of it”: everyone’s going to obey the law. “And the kings of the earth do bring their glory and honour into it”: we’re the kings of the earth that bring their glory into it. “And they shall bring the glory and honour of the nations into it”: this is why our economy is going to be the best, the highest. All wealth is coming to Jerusalem.

“And there shall in no wise enter into it any thing that defileth”: this is how you know the other nations are not the kings, because they’re not going to be entering into it, “but they which are written in the Lamb’s book of life.”

“The word that Isaiah the son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem.” Then the same words as Micah: “the mountain of the Lord’s house shall be established in the top of the mountains, and shall be exalted above the hills; and all nations shall flow unto it.” Everybody’s going to flow unto it.

Go back to Luke 19 to see who “all people” walking “in the name of his god” are: “Then came the first, saying, Lord, thy pound hath gained ten pounds. And he said unto him, Well, thou good servant: because thou hast been faithful in a very little, have thou authority over ten cities.” And to the second: “Be thou also over five cities.” Now you’re over these cities. The faithful servant set over a city is the god of that city, walking in the name of the Lord our God.

“I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.” Brother, you hear that? You are gods. So when Micah says every one will walk “in the name of his god”, it is speaking of us: set over ten cities, five cities, two cities, you are going to be a god again.

Who is this god? “I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.” Gods with a little g: the children of the Most High. Each people will walk in the name of its god, the Israelite set over them.

“Lord, thy pound hath gained ten pounds. And he said unto him, Well, thou good servant: because thou hast been faithful in a very little, have thou authority over ten cities.” When you have authority over ten cities, you are going to be their god.

“Be thou also over five cities.” Over five cities, you are their god, little g. That is Micah 4:5.

Read to bring about the pain. “I will go and return to my place”: God says he will go, return to his place, “till they acknowledge their offence”, until we acknowledge our offence, and our offence is us breaking the Commandments of God.

“And seek my face”: by him leaving us, the hope is it will cause us to seek his face; in other words, pay attention to the alarm clock. “In their affliction they will seek me early.” Affliction is pain. In our pain, our affliction, we will seek God early, and that is what is going to make us come and keep the Commandments.

You won’t do any kind of labor if you’re not pushed to do it, because labor is work. The man building the plane would love to fly one already built, but he had to decide it was worth putting in the pain and the time. Affliction is the pain, and the pain is what motivates our labor. Look at the pain and do nothing and you go into the garbage, you destroy yourself; but if the pain is on you and you don’t want to keep feeling it, you will do something to get out of it, and that is labor.

precepts.why:
Some of us ignore the pain like women during childbirth with epidurals and other things to mask it. God gave that pain to women as a reminder that they are to be obedient to their husbands, a reminder of how they messed up. This should be loved, because the consequence of not doing it is what’s jacking us up.

“Let the woman learn in silence with all subjection”: the Most High said for the women to learn from their husbands in silence, no back talk, no lip, when the man is telling them what to do out of the scriptures. On the job the white man says clean my windows with newspaper, and she’s in there cleaning it though it ain’t even in her job description, but when her husband asks her something she’s got a problem.

“But I suffer not a woman to teach, nor to usurp authority over the man, but to be in silence”: she is not supposed to be over the man, and God set that up. “For Adam was first formed, then Eve”: Adam was made first, Eve came from Adam, and everybody else came from Eve.

“And Adam was not deceived”, because Adam was already a god, a power in the earth; God made him lord over the earth and all his creatures. “But the woman being deceived was in the transgression”: she was deceived by Satan into wanting to be above Adam, in the transgression of listening to Satan to go against her husband. That’s why the Lord said she must learn in silence.

“Notwithstanding she shall be saved in childbearing, if they continue in faith and charity and holiness with sobriety”: if she follows what the Most High said she will be saved. If she’s running her mouth trying to be over her man she’s not going to be saved, simple as that. A lot of women with that big mouth driving their husbands crazy think they’re going to get the kingdom; they’re going to get death.

precepts.why:
Still dealing with the pain, the value and the gift of pain. “Unto the woman he said, I will greatly multiply thy sorrow and thy conception; in sorrow thou shalt bring forth children”: screaming and hollering, pain, pain, pain. It wasn’t supposed to be like this. Every time she has a baby it is a constant reminder of her disobedience against her husband. But he goes to the medical field for painkillers and epidurals so she doesn’t feel it, and she never understands the value of why God gave the pain, which lets her continue to be disobedient to her husband, and that abscess, that toothache, is going to be her death.

“And thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee”: that is what the pain is supposed to remind her of. The Bishop rightly pointed out, and he should know with twelve or fourteen children, that a woman in childbirth is in the most vulnerable position of her whole existence. There ain’t a damn thing she can do if the house catches on fire; she has to be there until it’s finished. God gave that excruciating pain to remind her of the Commandment to obey her husband, and “she shall be saved in childbearing” because in that childbearing she is supposed to remember this.

“And unto Adam he said, Because thou hast hearkened unto the voice of thy wife”: it was supposed to be him teaching her, but she ended up teaching him, usurping authority over him, and that’s out of order with the Lord. So the Lord gave him pain to remember: “cursed is the ground for thy sake; in sorrow shalt thou eat of it all the days of thy life.” “Thorns also and thistles shall it bring forth to thee”, “In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground”: work, work, work, when it was given to us in the beginning; until you die. Every time we work it is a reminder that we should not be listening to our wives.

Men need time to think on manly stuff and keep their minds on war, trying to get the kingdom, not carried off into conversations that most of the time ain’t righteous. That doesn’t mean she can’t say nothing; when she comes with scripture, she can speak.

“And Adam called his wife’s name Eve”: he named her, he got his sense back after getting that butt whipping from the Most High. “Because she was the mother of all living”: everybody came from her, Cain and Abel and all the rest of the people.

“Unto Adam also and to his wife did the Lord God make coats of skins, and clothed them”: that is when the law of sacrifice was introduced. The coats of skins are talking about the animals, and the very next chapter proves it.

What does it mean, all people will walk every one in the name of his god? “I have said, Ye are gods”: God said we are gods. “And all of you are children of the most High”: all of us are children of the Most High.

“But ye shall die like men”: we have died like men; we’re in slavery right now. “And fall like one of the princes”: we have fallen like one of the princes.

note.label: Micah 4: The Law Shall Go Forth of Zion

points: “In that day”: that is talking about the kingdom. “Will I assemble her that halteth”: halt means lame persons collectively, disabled, handicapped people who are crippled. This doesn’t mean that we are physically handicapped so much, but we are spiritually and mentally handicapped. We are all mentally and spiritually disabled, so we are the halt. We are the her that halteth, the disabled, and he is beginning now to assemble us.

“And I will gather her that is driven out”: the her that’s driven out is us. We’ve been driven out, scattered worldwide, and our goal, our mission, is to assemble the twelve tribes. That goal and that mission is too big to argue about on a street corner, too big to argue about a photograph.
“And her that I have afflicted”: God afflicted us. How? Slavery, oppression, colonialism. We’re the ones that God has afflicted.

“And I will make her that halted a remnant”: so we are the remnant. He’s not gathering all Israel, meaning he’s not gathering every Israelite on the planet. God is only gathering a remnant of the twelve tribes of Israel; a third will come up out of here and two-thirds are going to be put to death and die.

“And her that was cast far off a strong nation”: he’s going to make us into a strong nation. “And the Lord shall reign over them in mount Zion from henceforth, even for ever”: the Lord is going to reign over that mighty remnant of Israel.

“And thou, O tower of the flock”: Jerusalem is the tower of the flock, “the strong hold of the daughter of Zion,” because Jerusalem is going to be the capital of the planet Earth, the capital of the world.
“Unto thee shall it come, even the first dominion”: that’s Christ. We’re going to have the greatest King, and he’s going to rule from sea to sea. It’s going to come as the dominion of Christ.
“The kingdom shall come to the daughter of Jerusalem”: so the kingdom ain’t coming to everybody. The kingdom is only for Jerusalem, the daughter of Jerusalem.

“Now why dost thou cry out aloud?” The Lord is asking us. We cry for our sons and daughters being murdered, day by day, week by week, month by month, year by year, slain in the streets. We get tired, we are hurt, we are crying. But there’s a divine purpose behind all these deaths, and it’s only going to escalate until we acknowledge our offense.

“Is there no king in thee?” Our people say we got no king but Caesar, meaning the white man. Until our people realize that there is only one king, the Lord and Savior whom the world calls Jesus Christ, we will always suffer here in this land and worldwide.

“For pangs have taken thee as a woman in travail”: the pains that take hold of us like a woman in travail are the constant oppression, the tribulation that’s coming, all the day by day incidents we see on the news. Like a woman in travail: when is it going to end? It ain’t going to end until Israel wakes up and repents, till that number is reached.

“Be in pain”: this is a message to the teachers. Yes, it’s going to hurt. We must do this job regardless of what we go through in our personal lives, whether we have lost sons or daughters, mothers or fathers; no matter what, we must continue and push. “And labour to bring forth” means to work: labor to bring forth the remnant of Israel. “O daughter of Zion, like a woman in travail”: we’re going to have pains here and pains there in this truth.

“For now shalt thou go forth out of the city”: we left the city of Jerusalem, “and thou shalt dwell in the field,” meaning the world, “and thou shalt go even to Babylon,” and we’ve gone even to Babylon the great; that’s this place right here.

“There shalt thou be delivered”: we were not delivered in ancient Babylon; Persia took over and conquered. This Babylon is Babylon the great, the United States of America. “There the Lord shall redeem thee from the hand of thine enemies”: so the Lord ain’t redeeming all races, all people; he’s only redeeming the Israelites. From what? Their enemies. Some of our people don’t even believe they got enemies, it’s all love. It’s not all love: we have enemies who plot from sun up to sun down.

“Now also many nations are gathered against thee, that say, Let her be defiled”: let the Israelites be defiled. “And let our eye look upon Zion”: we are Zion. So the nations have gathered themselves against us.

“But they know not the thoughts of the Lord”: these nations who have looked upon us for evil, who have destroyed our people, who have consistently set up a political system of oppression nonstop, some we see and some we don’t, what they call systematic racism. The nations don’t know the thoughts of the Lord, with all their stupid religions. “Neither understand they his counsel”: his counsel is the Bible; these nations do not understand the Bible. “For he shall gather them as the sheaves into the floor.”

“Arise and thresh”: this is what the Lord is saying to us. Thresh means to separate grain from a plant, and it is a variant spelling of thrash: to beat a person or animal repeatedly and violently with a stick or whip, to hit something hard and repeatedly, to move in a violent and convulsive way. God is telling the Israelites to rise up and beat the hell out of the nations. Arise, wake up Israel. “O daughter of Zion”: we the daughter of Zion.

“For I will make thine horn iron”: he’s going to give us power. “And thou shalt beat in pieces many people”: we going to beat in pieces many people. I don’t know what Bible the Christians are reading.

“And I will consecrate their gain unto the Lord”: their gain is the forces of the Gentiles, their wealth, brought into Jerusalem. “And their substance unto the Lord of the whole earth”: that’s Christ, of that first dominion you read about in verse 8.

“But in the last days it shall come to pass, that the mountain of the house of the Lord shall be established in the top of the mountains”: it’s going to be the highest government on the planet earth. You’re going to have to look up to the kingdom of the Lord. “And it shall be exalted above the hills”, above all the other ones.

“And people shall flow unto it”: you’re going to have nations coming. You’re going to have Israelites coming up that we didn’t even know about, that the Lord is going to bring up. Nations are going to flow. We’re going to have the greatest and highest economy on planet earth.

Remember, we’re still talking about the thousand year reign. “And many nations shall come, and say, Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, and to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways”: they’re going to learn the law, “and we will walk in his paths”. “For the law shall go forth of Zion”: so whoever said the Lord has done away with it, we don’t know what you’re talking about. The law is going to be taught worldwide, “and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.”

“And he shall judge among many people, and rebuke strong nations afar off”: the nations that fall under that rebuke are going to be broken, and some of them are going to be enslaved. “And they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks”, meaningful instruments: “nation shall not lift up a sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.” There ain’t going to be no more war.
“But they shall sit every man under his vine and under his fig tree; and none shall make them afraid”: none is going to make us afraid.

“For all people will walk every one in the name of his god”: when you are set over ten cities, five cities, you are going to be a god again. Everybody’s going to walk in the name of his god. That’s why in Zechariah the ten men say, we’re going to take hold, we’re going to go with you: because we’re going to be the gods of those cities, “and we will walk in the name of the Lord our God for ever and ever.”

“In that day, saith the Lord, will I assemble her that halteth”: we’re the ones that halt, he’s going to assemble us. “And I will gather her that is driven out”: he’s going to gather us, because we’ve been driven out of Jerusalem, “and her that I have afflicted”: God has afflicted us.

“And I will make her that halted a remnant”: he’s going to make us a remnant, “and her that was cast far off a strong nation”: he’s going to make us a strong nation again. “And the Lord shall reign over them in mount Zion from henceforth, even for ever”: the Lord shall reign over us in Mount Zion. So we’re going to rejoice. That’s what the Bible is talking about.

“In the last days it shall come to pass, that the mountain of the house of the Lord shall be established in the top of the mountains, and it shall be exalted above the hills”. Our kingdom is going to be the highest government, exalted above all kingdoms.

“Many nations shall come, and say, Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord”. First it is the scattered Israelites who come; later the nations will be forced to come up and worship the King, as Zechariah 14 said. “For the law shall go forth of Zion”: the law is what will be taught.

“Nation shall not lift up a sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.” The only way there can be peace on earth is when the twelve tribes are reestablished under Christ; otherwise it is war after war. “They shall sit every man under his vine and under his fig tree; and none shall make them afraid”.
“For all people will walk every one in the name of his god”: god with a little g. That is us.
We want victory; we want to overcome.

“Be in pain, and labour to bring forth”: in this time, it’s prophesied, we must be in pain and labour to bring forth. Part of that pain means you might have to cut some of your loved ones off, the ones telling you don’t keep the Commandments. It hurts not talking to your mama no more; it hurts not being with your wife or your husband no more. But those of the spirit saying ‘I’m not keeping the Commandments and neither are you’ got to be cut off. Labour means work: you gotta work to bring forth this truth.

“O daughter of Zion, like a woman in travail.” A woman in travail has birthing pains: they may be spaced an hour apart, then thirty minutes apart, then minutes, then seconds, then the baby comes out. Likewise in this truth you’re gonna have days of pain, problems in this world, issues coming up, spaced years apart, months, weeks, days, hours, minutes apart; and then that destruction, and we are delivered.

“For now shalt thou go forth out of the city, and thou shalt dwell in the field, and thou shalt go even to Babylon”: that Babylon is Babylon the great. “There shalt thou be delivered.” That’s the evidence: we weren’t delivered from ancient Babylon by the Lord, but we’re going to be delivered from this Babylon. “There the Lord shall redeem thee from the hand of thine enemies.” That didn’t happen in ancient Babylon: Persia conquered them, and we went into the Persian captivity. So this is about the Lord redeeming us.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

points: This scripture runs all through the rest of the class, taken piece by piece, because it shows the whole setup of how we are supposed to move. What we need to understand is that this whole system has been designed to keep us as slaves, and that is the war happening in the earth right now: war in heaven and in earth.

“For now shalt thou go forth out of the city”: that city is Babylon the great. “And thou shalt go even to Babylon; there shalt thou be delivered; there the Lord shall redeem thee from the hand of thine enemies.” In Babylon the great we shall be delivered. Babylon the actual country, the kingdom, never delivered us from the hand of our enemies; we went from Babylon to Persia in captivity. So the Babylon spoken of here is Babylon the great.

“Be in pain”: pain of the mind, looking at the reality that caused us not to evolve as a people. Outside of the small steps of the Civil Rights and things of that nature, we are still in relatively the same predicament we were in 1963 in how we think as a collective. Twenty years after that, 1983, the same mentality, and from there up to now things have gotten worse: black folks with a white mind. In order to fix a problem you have to know its cause; you have to get into the deep bowels of the issues causing the sick behavior, and we are taught to ignore that. You have to pay attention to the rottenness that’s in us. If you don’t talk to your fathers and your elders, every generation has to start from scratch.

The feeling of pain is given to us by God, and there is a benefit to it. When you have pain in your teeth, it tells you something is wrong with the condition of your teeth; ignore it and it gets much worse, and an abscess with poison in the root can even lead to death. Pain is an alarm clock that seeks to get your attention. There is an abscess in our history, an abscess in our growth, and because we ignored the footsteps behind us we end up walking right back into it. The way we think, the exaggerated startle response, post-traumatic slave syndrome, all of it curtails our progress, and if we don’t go back and find out exactly what happened and how, we stay in it.

Painkillers only silence the alarm clock: get high, get drunk, and you wake up in a stupor still with a damn toothache. Christianity does the same thing. It doesn’t deal with the reason we went into the church in the first place; it makes us feel good for the moment, but we come back out and our homes are still broken, our children still out of order, our men still sent to jail in record numbers. Unemployment, drug addiction, mental illness, homelessness and illiteracy are all still there, because the cause is never addressed, so the pain constantly reoccurs. Immediate gratification is a painkiller; addressing the problem is how you alleviate the pain.

It is not enough to say we went into slavery because we broke the Commandments and leave it at that. Keeping the Commandments is a must, but it won’t be seen that way unless we understand the consequences of not keeping them. Tell somebody all day to brush their teeth after every meal and they might not listen; once they get that pain in the mouth they remember, because that’s history. That’s what Deuteronomy the 28th chapter is all about. Pain is pushback: if you know sticking your hand in the fire will burn you, you have enough sense not to go there, but take a painkiller and you won’t feel your arm burning up. In this wicked society full of temptation, without the pain behind breaking the Commandments you will be encouraged to break them.

Pains and judgments are what cause us to acknowledge our misbehavior, the way parents chastise children. A child that is never chastened grows up spoiled, thinking there’s no consequence for anything, and ends up dead; ignore the pain and you end up with nothing but gums. Pain is what motivates our labor. Look back at the atrocities we went through, see how they messed us up, and we have no choice but to say we got to do something about this: restore the decayed state of our people, as they did in the Maccabean period looking at the pain of the nation of Israel being destroyed.

“And labour to bring forth”: labor is work. In the book Black Men: Obsolete, Single, Dangerous, a man tells how his mother bought him a blue plastic airplane with blue wheels and a string to pull it across the floor, while in Dearborn, Michigan, where the movers and shakers of the automobile industry lived and where black women did day work cleaning white folks’ homes, there were no five and dime stores, only craft shops. There white parents bought their sons airplanes in boxes, wooden parts, directions, glue and small engines; the son assembled it over a day or two, took it outside, and it would fly. That is pain and labor, not immediate gratification. Through it the child learned work ethics, discipline, priority, decision making, science and math principles.

The black child bought the plane already assembled and hoped it rolled on the floor like a car or a truck. He was learning to be a consumer who depended on others to build the plane for him, being trained to use his body from the neck down, while the white upper class boy was taught to build things and run things from the neck up. That is how black people are: 1.4 trillion dollars in consumerism, waiting for somebody to bring us a car, a house. Give this man reparations and he won’t do nothing but put rims on the wheels of the plane, because his education won’t go beyond that.

Everybody has 24 hours in a day; discipline is how you use your minutes. Trim the BS, remove frolic and stupidness, slice out the time, and when the hard work is finished you sit back and appreciate the work of your hands. God created the heavens and the earth from what was in his thoughts first, and man was formulated to do the same: before Adam made a chair or a house or a covering for shame, it had to be in his mind, and then he used his hands to bring the elements out of the earth. Faith without works is dead, faith without discipline is dead. People can only see what was in your head once you put hands to it and bring it into existence.

To see a man defiled and destroyed: that is the nations, all of them.

The triad told the drug dealer the same thing: black people are the trendsetters, but they have no unity, very easy to break up. A nation divided shall not stand, and that is why Esau divides us in the colonies we were born in.
